title: REDUCing ChEmotherapy intensity for aged or vulnerable patients with advanced or metastatic LUNG cancer, a phase 3 randomized study
official: REDUCing ChEmotherapy intensity for aged or vulnerable patients with advanced or metastatic LUNG cancer, a phase 3 randomized study (REDUCE-LUNG)
summary: Main objective: To assess the benefit in survival without severe toxicities offered by a reduced-intensity treatment regimen consisting of two induction cycles of chemoimmunother-apy (platin-doublet chemotherapy combined with pembrolizumab) followed by maintenance pembrolizumab (±pemetrexed), compared to the standard regimen of four induction cycles in vulnera-ble patients (aged ≥70 years and/or with ECOG PS 2) with metastatic or locally ad-vanced NSCLC not amenable to local ab-lative treatment.
conditions: Aged patients or ECOG PS 2 patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients aged ≥70 years with ECOG performance status (PS) 0 to 2, or patients 18-69 years-old and ECOG PS 2.
2. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must have a negative urine or se-rum β-HCG pregnancy test within 7 days prior to registration. If the urine test is positive or cannot be confirmed as negative, a serum pregnancy test will be required. Sexually active female patients must agree to use two methods of effective contraception (e.g., one being a barrier method) or to abstain from sexual activity during the clinical investigation and for at least 6 months after the last dose of the investigational treatment.
3. Men participating in the study must agree to use a condom during the clinical investigation and for at least 6 months after the last dose of the investigational treatment. It is also recommended that their partners use a highly effective method of contraception for the same duration.
4. Affiliation to a social security system or beneficiary of equivalent coverage
5. Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
6. Metastatic or locally advanced not amendable to local ablative treatment (surgery or radiation)
7. Absence of genomic alterations that enable targeted treatment in first line (e.g., but not limited to alterations in EGFR, ALK, ROS1, RET, BRAF V600E, or NTRK)
8. No prior systemic treatment for metastatic NSCLC. Patients may have re-ceived systemic treatments for localized NSCLC, with a minimum 6-month de-lay since the last treatment received.
9. Patients with measurable disease as per RECIST v1.1 criteria
10. Adequate organ and bone marrow functions for platinum-based chemothera-py according to local standards, including: o	Hematological parameters: hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L, platelets ≥100 × 10⁹/L. o	Hepatic parameters: total bilirubin ≤1.5 × ULN (upper limit normal) un-less due to Gilbert’s syndrome, AST/ALT ≤3 × ULN (or ≤5 × ULN if liver metastases are present). o	Renal function: estimated creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min (using MDRD formula), or ≥45 mL/min if the patient will receive pemetrexed.
11. Ability to comply with the study protocol and scheduled visits.
12. Signed informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. ECOG PS 3 or 4.
2. History of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organized pneumonia (i.e., obliterat-ing bronchiolitis), drug-induced lung disease, or active signs of pneumonia, pulmonary infiltration (regardless of cause except cancer) detected on the baseline chest CT scan.
3. Any condition that represents a contraindication to any of the chemotherapy agents or pembrolizumab according to local guidelines or the national pre-scription guidelines
4. Any situation for which exclusive palliative care intervention is recommended.
5. Patient under guardianship or deprived of liberty by a judicial or administra-tive decision, or incapable of providing informed consent.
6. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women intending to become pregnant during the clinical investigation.
7. Known hypersensitivity to the investigational products or any excipients
8. Any condition that, in the investigator’s opinion, could jeopardize the safety of the patient or interfere with protocol compliance and study outcomes.
9. Concomitant treatment with another experimental treatment or participation in another clinical trial.
10. Symptomatic brain metastases requiring increasing doses of steroids. Pa-tients with asymptomatic brain metastases or with stable symptomatic brain metastases not requiring steroids may be included.
11. Patients who are expected to require any other form of systemic antineo-plastic therapy while on study. Local radiation to symptomatic tumor lesions is allowed, unless the lesion is defined as a target lesion. No wash out period between radiation of any organ and the start of the trial treatment is required.
12. Corticosteroids at a dose greater than 20 mg per day of prednisone or equiva-lent.
13. Ongoing immunosuppressive systemic therapy (e.g., cyclophosphamide, aza-thioprine, methotrexate, thalidomide, anti-TNF agents).
14. Administration of a live attenuated vaccine within the 4 weeks before day 1 of Cycle 1 or administration of a live attenuated vaccine planned for the duration of the study. Other kinds of influenza and/or COVID vaccines may be applied without restrictions.
15. History of any other hematologic or primary solid tumor malignancy unless in remission for at least 2 years and without specific treatment. Exceptions in-clude adequately treated basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or in situ carcinoma.
16. Severe uncontrolled comorbidities, including significant cardiovascular dis-ease (e.g., myocardial infarction in the last 6 months, severe or unstable angi-na pectoris, congestive heart failure), active or uncontrolled infection including chronic hepatitis B or C or HIV (Individuals with a positive HIV test at screen-ing are eligible, provided they are stable on anti-retroviral therapy, have a CD4 count >= 200/µL, and have an undetectable viral load).
17. History of autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppression (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis) or active autoimmune disease likely to be exacerbated by immune checkpoint inhibitors. Patients with a history of autoimmune hypothyroidism treated with a stable dose of hormone replacement therapy are eligible. Patients with diabetes treated with insulin are eligible
